newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks halt slide on Dow in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks halt slide on Dow in dull trade.

text.p: Mexican stocks pared earlier losses, but closed down on Monday after what traders said was a listless session in which share prices drifted in line with the Dow Jones.
"We had a really slack day today, one of the worst in a long time, with scant turnover and not even much same-day buy-sell dealing," a desk trader.

The leading IPC share index .MXX ended down 15.16 points, or 0.40 percent, at 3,760.55. Trading volume .TV.MX was lackluster at 61.3 million shares traded, of which cross trades accounted for almost one-half.
Traders said dealing was in the doldrums due to the lack of foreign brokers in the market.
Analysts and dealers said the IPC rebounded from a session low of 3,735.98 points on light last-minute bargain-hunting prompted by a recovery on Wall Street.
The Dow Jones ended up 0.29 percent at 6,955.48 points after being in negative turf for most of the day.

"Buyers stepped in close to 3,730 points because the bourse respected support there and confirmed resistance at 3,750 points," said Hector Jimenez, a technical analyst at the Inverlat brokerage in Mexico City.
"What helped us was the (upward) adjustment in the Dow Jones and the price of U.S. long bonds," Jimenez added.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond pared earlier falls and closed off 6/32 to yield 6.96 percent.
The broad market echoed the downward trend in blue chips. Out of a total of 95 stocks traded, sliders outnumbered gainers by 49 to 25.
Telecomms firm Telmex L shares, off four centavos at 15.86 pesos, weighed most heavily on the market, followed by retail stock Cifra C shares, which fell 22 centavos to 10.84 pesos.
Telmex L and Cifra C shares together accounted for one-third of all shares traded. Traders said Cifra C traded relatively heavily on a company buyback.
Debt-ridden holding company Sidek headed the prominent gainers .PG.MX, up two centavos to 46 centavos, on what dealers said was low-volume speculative buying.
Traders said other leading gainers and decliners .PL.MX were shares whose prices had moved after thin-volume and unrepresentative deals.
Dealers expected share prices on Tuesday to respond to the outlook for the primary Cetes auction to be held that evening, and said they also awaited January industrial output figures.
"I think some are waiting for prices to fall further before buying. It seems that we have already gone on vacation," one trader said, referring to forthcoming pubic holidays.
